title: A TV is approved from a phone
description: Serves "Joining and signing in are easy and safe.".
acceptanceCriteria: Only the TV starts it; the code is single-use and short-lived, and guessing it is bounded.

A phone that scans the TV's code opens the approval in Octave with the code filled in; it shows the device, the network (same as the phone or not) and the code to match, with Decline as prominent as Approve.
A viewer signed out on the phone signs in there first (password or single sign-on).
The TV gets a viewer-only sign-in of its own, listed and revocable (JS-042).

Approving a device, and any action that creates a credential or sets a password, needs a fresh sign-in the server checks: proof that covers that one action, works once and expires within minutes. A web session cannot approve a device without it (#301).
With real processes, each step is answered by a different api replica.
Every capability it adds is in the published contract (JS-183) and passes its conformance check.

The approval's password is checked under the signed-in phone's own known-device bound only, never the bound per name or per address. Tries at the name from elsewhere, and other people's wrong passwords from the same address, never stop a viewer approving a TV.
notes: Quick Connect goes at the cutover, so the server side of this lands before it. Viewers use it once Octave has an approval screen; until then a TV signs in by password. Amended 2026-11-27 by D-20261127-tv-approval-phone-bound and D-20261127-tv-approval-own-device-only, decided by the product owner: dependsOn adds JS-216 (beside JS-184), and criterion 8 is added. docs/access.md, written by this task: "A TV approval's password counts only toward the approving device's own bound." A TV whose answer was lost asks again and gets the same sign-in, as Quick Connect does (D-20261127-tv-code-token-sealed).
